f. Work Trips
Approximately 265,620 daily work trips were generated from persons living within the Regional Core in 1970. Of these, about one-third originated in the Wilshire District, one-fourth were from the Holly-wood area, and one-eighth or less began in the remaining Community Plan areas. Overall, auto travel to work was favored five-to-one over public transit. Only in the more centrally located, lower income Westlake and Central City communities did public transit provide a major proportion of work trips for persons living in each of those communities. Outlying suburbanites use of public transportation dropped to 3% in North Hollywood and Sherman Oaks-Studio City, while their auto use exceeded 90% of work trips. These results are shown in Figure V.11.
The magnitude of pedestrian and other means of work travel in the Central City, comprising 43% of such trips, indicated a high proportion of individuals living near their places of work.
